title: Fang Bo climbs 94 places to world No 66 after his WTT Contender Istanbul title
seo_title: World rankings: Fang Bo climbs 94 places to No 66
description: Fang Bo is back in the world top 100 at 66th after his Istanbul title, a comeback he pays for himself, while the top 25 men and top 23 women do not move.
standfirst: The 34-year-old gained 400 points for his first title since 2013, won with a neck injury and painkillers, while Kang Dongsoo and Ryoichi Yoshiyama also climb and the top of both rankings stays put.

videos.title: Fang Bo v Kang Dongsoo, men's singles final

body: Fang Bo has climbed 94 places to 66th in the world after winning WTT Contender Istanbul, back in the top 100 seven months after he came out of retirement to play for Kazakhstan.

The 34-year-old gained 400 points for the title and now has 567, up from 167 when he was ranked 160th. The ITTF ranking for week 47, published on Monday, leaves the top 25 men and the top 23 women unchanged, so the biggest movements are lower down and come mostly from Istanbul.
## A comeback paid for himself

Fang, who won a world team title with China in 2016 and reached the singles final at the 2015 World Championships, retired from the national team in 2021. He became a streamer and started his own table tennis club before announcing in April that he would return for Kazakhstan, under terms that keep him out of the Olympics, the World Championships and the World Cup.

He told The Paper that the idea came from a remark by a Kazakh federation official during the President's Cup in Kazakhstan. "It was just a joke, and I took it seriously," he said (translated from Chinese). Once he was sure his company would keep running smoothly, he decided that "playing is more important than money".

The money is a real cost. Fang has no team doctor and no support staff, buys his own rubbers and books his own hotels, and has said in a video that one European tournament costs him about 150,000 yuan in flights, hotels and expenses, far more than the prize money for a first-round exit.
## Painkillers in Istanbul

The title came at a physical price too. Li Liangfu, who coaches Fang from the side of the court, wrote after the final that Fang hurt his neck stretching for a ball in his first doubles match in Istanbul and thought about withdrawing. He needed 30 to 45 minutes of treatment before every match and took painkillers each day.

"Fang Bo hardly trained before his matches, because he couldn't afford to use up any more muscle," Li wrote (translated from Chinese). The Paper reported that Fang also had an injection in his chest before he left for Europe.

Fang's own post after the final was a video of the trophy and a line that has since trended on Chinese social media: "I'm not one of the chosen few, but I'm no ordinary player." He had described the comeback earlier as harder on his nerves than his first career. "I should be at the stage of enjoying it, but I'm more nervous than before, I can't even sleep," he wrote. "But I like this kind of tough challenge. The story is far from over."

His return started slowly, with defeats in qualifying at his first two events, and he did not win a main-draw match until WTT Contender Almaty in September, where he reached the quarter-finals. He has said he sees the comeback as a project of at least two or three years, aimed at earning enough points to play every level of WTT event.
## The other climbers

Kang Dongsoo, the South Korean defender Fang [beat 4-1 in the Istanbul final](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-finals-fang-bo-honoka-hashimoto-titles.html), climbs 52 places to 68th on 542 points. Ricardo Walther, the German Fang beat from two games down in the semi-finals, rises 55 places to 88th.

Japan's Ryoichi Yoshiyama, 22, reaches a career-best 49th from 62nd after his run to the semi-finals, which included [a quarter-final win over China's Li Tianyang](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-quarter-finals-hirano-yoshiyama-china-out.html). Lubomir Jancarik of the Czech Republic, a quarter-finalist, goes from 49th to 43rd.

At the top, Sora Matsushima stays No 1 on 7,598 points ahead of his Japan teammate Tomokazu Harimoto, with Félix Lebrun third and Wang Chuqin fourth. Lin Shidong is 10th, which leaves China with two men in the top 10.
## The women's ranking
Wang Manyu stays No 1 on 9,265 points, ahead of Sun Yingsha on 8,575 and Miwa Harimoto on 6,889. Honoka Hashimoto, the Istanbul champion, stays 14th, her total rising from 2,924 to 3,054 points.

Miu Hirano, who lost to Hashimoto in the Istanbul semi-finals, moves up one place to 24th and swaps places with China's Qin Yuxuan. Saki Shibata, a quarter-finalist in Istanbul, climbs 14 places to 58th, and China's 20-year-old Zong Geman rises 16 places to 60th.
## What comes next

Fang went straight on to WTT Star Contender Muscat, where he plays Turkey's Abdullah Yigenler in the first qualifying round at 2.45pm UK time on Monday. On Tuesday he partners Austria's Sofia Polcanova in mixed doubles qualifying, and Kang plays China's Zhou Jinquan in the second round of singles qualifying. Muscat ends on Saturday 21 November, and its points will count in next week's ranking.
